cases.sentence: Если князь Андрей сам не уведомлял ее, то это княжна Марья объясняла или тем, что он был слишком слаб, чтобы писать, или тем, что он считал для нее и для своего сына этот ___ слишком трудным и опасным.
cases.explain: «длинный переезд» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: When Princess Márya heard from Nikoláy that her brother was with the Rostóvs at Yaroslávl she at once prepared to go there, in spite of her aunt’s efforts to dissuade her—and not merely to go herself but to take her nephew with her. Whether it were difficult or easy, possible or impossible, she did not ask and did not want to know: it was her duty, not only to herself, to be near her brother who was perhaps dying, but to do everything possible to take his son to him, and so she prepared to set off. That she had not heard from Prince Andréy himself, Princess Márya attributed to his being too weak to write or to his considering the long journey too hard and too dangerous for her and his son.

cases.sentence: С ней ехали m-lle Bourienne, Николушка с гувернером, ___, три девушки, Тихон, молодой лакей и гайдук, которого тетка отпустила с нею.
cases.explain: «старая няня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: In a few days Princess Márya was ready to start. Her equipages were the huge family coach in which she had traveled to Vorónezh, a semiopen trap, and a baggage cart. With her traveled Mademoiselle Bourienne, Nikolúshka and his tutor, her old nurse, three maids, Tíkhon, and a young footman and courier her aunt had sent to accompany her.

cases.sentence: С ней ехали m-lle Bourienne, Николушка с гувернером, старая няня, три девушки, Тихон, ___ и гайдук, которого тетка отпустила с нею.
cases.explain: «молодой лакей» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Во время этого ___, m-llе Bourienne, Десаль и прислуга княжны Марьи были удивлены ее твердостью духа и деятельностью.
cases.explain: «трудного путешествия» — after the preposition «во», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: During this difficult journey Mademoiselle Bourienne, Dessalles, and Princess Márya’s servants were astonished at her energy and firmness of spirit. She went to bed later and rose earlier than any of them, and no difficulties daunted her. Thanks to her activity and energy, which infected her fellow travelers, they approached Yaroslávl by the end of the second week.

cases.sentence: Благодаря ее деятельности и энергии, возбуждавших ее спутников, к концу ___ они подъезжали к Ярославлю.
cases.explain: «второй недели» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: Николай ни одним словом не намекнул на то, что теперь (в случае выздоровления князя Андрея) ___ между ним и Наташей могли возобновиться, но княжна Марья видела по его лицу, что он знал и думал это.
cases.explain: «прежние отношения» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The last days of her stay in Vorónezh had been the happiest of her life. Her love for Rostóv no longer tormented or agitated her. It filled her whole soul, had become an integral part of herself, and she no longer struggled against it. Latterly she had become convinced that she loved and was beloved, though she never said this definitely to herself in words. She had become convinced of it at her last interview with Nikoláy, when he had come to tell her that her brother was with the Rostóvs. Not by a single word had Nikoláy alluded to the fact that Prince Andréy’s relations with Natásha might, if he recovered, be renewed, but Princess Márya saw by his face that he knew and thought of this. Yet in spite of that, his relation to her—considerate, delicate, and loving—not only remained unchanged, but it sometimes seemed to Princess Márya that he was even glad that the family connection between them allowed him to express his friendship more freely. She knew that she loved for the first and only time in her life and felt that she was beloved, and was happy in regard to it.

cases.sentence: Но подъезжая к Ярославлю, когда открылось опять то, что̀ могло предстоять ей и уже не через много дней, а нынче вечером, волнение княжны Марьи дошло до ___.
cases.explain: «крайних пределов» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: As always happens when traveling, Princess Márya thought only of the journey itself, forgetting its object. But as she approached Yaroslávl the thought of what might await her there—not after many days, but that very evening—again presented itself to her and her agitation increased to its utmost limit.

cases.sentence: Княжна Марья испуганно-вопросительно смотрела в его лицо, не понимая, почему он не отвечал на ___: что́ брат?
cases.explain: «главный вопрос» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Princess Márya looked at him with frightened inquiry, not understanding why he did not reply to what she chiefly wanted to know: how was her brother? Mademoiselle Bourienne put that question for her.

cases.sentence: Княжна взбежала по лестнице, притворно улыбавшаяся девушка сказала: сюда, сюда! и княжна очутилась, в передней перед старою женщиной с ___ лица, которая с растроганным выражением быстро шла ей навстречу.
cases.explain: «восточным типом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The carriage door was opened. On the left there was water—a great river—and on the right a porch. There were people at the entrance: servants, and a rosy girl with a large plait of black hair, smiling as it seemed to Princess Márya in an unpleasantly affected way.

cases.sentence: Она, сама не зная как, проговорила какие-то учтивые ___, в том же тоне, в котором были те, которые ей говорили, и спросила: — что̀ он?
cases.explain: «французские слова» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Despite her excitement, Princess Márya realized that this was the countess and that it was necessary to say something to her. Hardly knowing how she did it, she contrived to utter a few polite phrases in French in the same tone as those that had been addressed to her, and asked: “How is he?”

cases.sentence: О, какой ___!
cases.explain: «прелестный мальчик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “One moment, Princess, one moment, my dear! Is this his son?” said the countess, turning to Nikolúshka who was coming in with Dessalles. “There will be room for everybody, this is a big house. Oh, what a lovely boy!”

cases.sentence: ___ вошел в комнату, приветствуя княжну.
cases.explain: «Старый граф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The countess took Princess Márya into the drawing room, where Sónya was talking to Mademoiselle Bourienne. The countess caressed the boy, and the old count came in and welcomed the princess. He had changed very much since Princess Márya had last seen him. Then he had been a brisk, cheerful, self-assured old man; now he seemed a pitiful, bewildered person. While talking to Princess Márya he continually looked round as if asking everyone whether he was doing the right thing. After the destruction of Moscow and of his property, thrown out of his accustomed groove he seemed to have lost the sense of his own significance and to feel that there was no longer a place for him in life.

cases.sentence: Но не успела княжна взглянуть на лицо этой Наташи, как она поняла, что это был ее ___ по горю, и потому ее друг.
cases.explain: «искренний товарищ» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: But hardly had the princess looked at Natásha’s face before she realized that here was a real comrade in her grief, and consequently a friend. She ran to meet her, embraced her, and began to cry on her shoulder.

cases.sentence: Чуткая княжна Марья с ___ на лицо Наташи поняла всё это, и с горестным наслаждением плакала на ее плече.
cases.explain: «первого взгляда» — after the preposition «с», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Princess Márya, with her acute sensibility, understood all this at the first glance at Natásha’s face, and wept on her shoulder with sorrowful pleasure.

cases.sentence: Чуткая княжна Марья с первого взгляда на лицо Наташи поняла всё это, и с ___ плакала на ее плече.
cases.explain: «горестным наслаждением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Princess Márya, with her acute sensibility, understood all this at the first glance at Natásha’s face, and wept on her shoulder with sorrowful pleasure.

cases.sentence: Губа Наташи вдруг дрогнула, ___ образовались вокруг ее рта, и она, зарыдав, закрыла лицо руками.
cases.explain: «уродливые морщины» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Natásha was gazing at her, but seemed afraid and in doubt whether to say all she knew or not; she seemed to feel that before those luminous eyes which penetrated into the very depths of her heart, it was impossible not to tell the whole truth which she saw. And suddenly, Natásha’s lips twitched, ugly wrinkles gathered round her mouth, and covering her face with her hands she burst into sobs.

cases.sentence: Они посидели несколько времени внизу подле его комнаты с тем, чтобы перестать плакать и войти к нему с ___.
cases.explain: «спокойными лицами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: They sat a little while downstairs near his room till they had left off crying and were able to go to him with calm faces.

cases.sentence: Наташа рассказала, что первое время была опасность от ___ и страдания, но у Троицы это прошло, и доктор боялся одного — Антонова огня.
cases.explain: «горячечного состояния» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Natásha told her that at first there had been danger from his feverish condition and the pain he suffered, but at Tróitsa that had passed and the doctor had only been afraid of gangrene. That danger had also passed. When they reached Yaroslávl the wound had begun to fester (Natásha knew all about such things as festering) and the doctor had said that the festering might take a normal course. Then fever set in, but the doctor had said the fever was not very serious. “But two days ago this suddenly happened,” said Natásha, struggling with her sobs. “I don’t know why, but you will see what he is like.”
